```{r}
dist <- list()
dist_name <- c(
  "0"  = "none",
  "10" = "other",
  "20" = "cut",
  "30" = "road",
  "40" = "fire",
  "50" = "biotic"
)

dist.forecastparams <- list()

count <- 1
for (dclass in names(dist.priors)) {
  dist.name <- as.character(dist_name[dclass])
  nclust <- length(dist.priors[[dclass]]$means)
  
  for (i in 1:nclust) {
    dist.forecastparams[[count]] <- list()
    dist.forecastparams[[count]]$mu0 <- c(0.2, dist.priors[[dclass]]$means[i])
    dist.forecastparams[[count]]$V0 <- diag(c(0.04, dist.priors[[dclass]]$vars[i]))
    dist.forecastparams[[count]]$name <- paste0(dist.name, i)
    count <- count + 1
  }
}
```

```{r}
Rw <- (84*B2C*1000*1e-4)^2 ## Observation Error: Kennedy et al 2018 Environ. Res. Lett. 13 025004; Fig 2 RMSE
## units: Mg/ha -> kg/m2
print(dim(Yw))
## grab the distribution of AGB for the first time point from all pixels
AGBprior <- Yw[,1]
ne = length(AGBprior) ## number of ensemble members

## spin up
PARlong <- as.vector(t(rad)) # concatenate PAR time series for each site into one vector
spin = VSEM(theta,PARlong) # Question: why run VSEM on the concatenated PAR? What is theta?
thin = seq(nrow(spin)/2,nrow(spin),length=ne)
spinIC = spin[thin,2:4] # select ne samples from the spin-up 
#for(i in 2:4){
#  hist(spin[thin,i],type='l')
#}

## disturbance recovery trajectory
nNBG = 200 ## years
NBG <- array(NA,c(ne,nNBG,3))
for(i in 1:ne){
  param = theta
  param[9:11] <- spinIC[i,]*c(0.01,1,0.01) ## set leaf and wood to 1% (simulate disturbance)
  raw = VSEM(param,PARlong[1:(nNBG*365.25)]) # simulate for nNBG years
  NBG[i,,] = raw[round(seq(365,nNBG*365.25,length=nNBG)),2:4]  ## grab pools at the end of each year
}
  
## for each AGBprior, grab the matching leaf and soil
ICprior <- matrix(NA,ne,3)
age = rep(NA,ne)
for(i in 1:ne){
  age[i] <- which.min((AGBprior[i]-NBG[i,,3])^2) # age = year in the disturbance recover trajectory where the simulated site has similar AGB to the AGB prior information
  ICprior[i,] <- c(NBG[i,age[i],1:2],AGBprior[i]) # use AGBprior for the model ICs
}
hist(age)
colnames(ICprior) <- c("Cv","Cs","CR") 
pairs(ICprior)
```

```{r}

## ---- Site-independent setup (computed once) --------------------------------
## Number of disturbance sub-classes and number of assimilation years.
n.dist = length(dist.forecastparams)
NT = floor(ncol(rad)/365)

## Background disturbance-type probability per forecast component, by matching
## the component's name to one of "other"/"cut"/"fire"/"biotic".
distname.toidx <- list("other"=2, "cut"=3, "fire"=4, "biotic"=5)
dist.prior.probs <- sapply(dist.forecastparams, function(x) {
  name <- x$name
  for (d in names(distname.toidx)) {
    if (grepl(d, name)) {
      return(d.prior[distname.toidx[[d]]])
    }
  }
})

## Diagonal process-error covariance (per-pool SDs) and prior process-precision
## gamma params (a, b) = (shape, rate). Both site-independent.
Q = diag(c(Ql,Qsoil,Qw)^2)
a <- 1/0.1172475
b <- 1
gamInit <- c(a, b)

## Default heteroskedastic Rparams for GEDI (slope, intercept).
Rparams.GEDI.het <- c(0.01331, 0.09761)
Rparams.GEDI.fixed <- c(0.0000000, 0.8848249)
Rparams.Landtrendr.het <- c(0.013310, 3.012645)
Rparams.Landtrendr.fixed <- c(0.000, 3.79986)

## ---- Per-site argument builder ---------------------------------------------
## make_or_args(site, useDistProduct) assembles the site-specific inputs to
## ORJointUpdate: the (n.dist+1) x NT prior probability matrix p.dist (row 1 =
## undisturbed, rows 2.. = disturbance sub-classes), the bundled disturb.params,
## the NT x 3 observation matrix Y (wood-pool obs in column 3), and the PAR
## driver for that site. Relies on the site-independent globals above plus
## d.prior, dist.priors, dist.forecastparams, dextract, Yw and rad.
make_or_args <- function(site, useDistProduct = TRUE) {
  ## Initialize every year with the background prior (same column for all t).
  p.dist <- array(NA, dim = c(n.dist + 1, NT))
  for (t in 1:NT) {
    p.dist[1:(n.dist+1), t] <- as.numeric(c(d.prior[1], unlist(dist.prior.probs)))
  }

  ## If using the disturbance product, override the prior in years where a
  ## disturbance was detected at this site: replace that class's prior with the
  ## user's-accuracy estimate (Kennedy et al. 2015 table 6). Then give each
  ## component a share of the disturbance probability proportional to its weight,
  ## and the disturbed values to sum to 1 if they sum to greater than 1, and else
  ## set the undisturbed value to 1 - p(disturbed).
  if (useDistProduct) {
    distidx.toname = list("10"="OTHER", "20"="CUT", "40"="FIRE", "50"="PEST")
    users_accuracy = c(1-d.prior[1], .77, .92, .77, .78, .78) ## 0 = none, 10 = other, 20 = cut, 30 = road, 40 = fire, 50 = biotic
    weights <- unlist(sapply(dist.priors, function(x) x$weights))

    for (d in seq(names(dist.priors))) {
      d.name <- names(dist.priors)[d]
      has.dist <- which(dextract[site,] == d.name)
      if (length(has.dist) > 0) {
        is.dist <- which(names(dist.prior.probs) == distidx.toname[[d.name]]) + 1
        p.dist[is.dist, has.dist] <- users_accuracy[dextract[site, has.dist]/10 + 1]
      }
    }

    ## Combine into a per-year categorical prior. Keep the within-class `weights`
    ## (mclust mixture proportions, sum to 1 per class) so a class's probability is
    ## split across its cluster components without over-counting. Then set the
    ## undisturbed prior to the *remaining* mass (= 1 - product accuracy in flagged
    ## years, = background otherwise) instead of renormalizing against the large
    ## background undisturbed prior, so the raw disturbance-product probability is
    ## preserved rather than diluted.
    for (j in 1:ncol(p.dist)) {
      p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] <- p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] * weights   # split class prob across clusters
      dist.mass <- sum(p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j])
      if (dist.mass > 1) {                                           # guard: cap total disturbed mass at 1
        p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] <- p.dist[2:(n.dist+1), j] / dist.mass
        dist.mass <- 1
      }
      p.dist[1, j] <- 1 - dist.mass                                  # undisturbed = remaining mass
    }
  }

  ## Bundle the disturbance prior + per-class forecast params.
  disturb.params <- list(
    p = p.dist,
    n = n.dist,
    vals = dist.forecastparams,
    alloc.soil = 0.05
  )

  ## NT x 3 observation matrix with the wood-pool obs in column 3.
  Y <- matrix(NA, NT, 3)
  Y[1:ncol(Yw), 3] <- Yw[site, ]

  list(Y = Y, disturb.params = disturb.params, PAR = rad[site, ], site = site)
}
```


```{r}
# Helper functions for ORJointUpdate

KalmanUpdate <- function(m, C, H, R, y) {
  S <- H %*% C %*% t(H) + R
  K <- C %*% t(H) %*% solve(S)
  m_hat <- m + K %*% (y - H %*% m)
  C_hat <- (diag(nrow(C)) - K %*% H) %*% C
  L_hat <- dnorm(y, mean = H %*% m, sd = sqrt(S))
  
  return(list(m_hat=m_hat, C_hat=C_hat, L_hat=L_hat))
}

gauss_laguerre_rate <- function(n, alpha, beta) {
  gq <- gauss.quad(n, kind = "laguerre", alpha = alpha)  # weight x^alpha e^{-x}
  list(nodes   = gq$nodes / beta,
       weights = gq$weights / beta^(alpha + 1))
}

integrate_gl <- function(f, gq) sum(gq$weights * sapply(gq$nodes, f))

# solve the following equation for a and fixed c using newton's method:
# digamma(a) - log(a) = c
solve_digamma_log <- function(c, tol = 1e-12, maxiter = 100, a.max = 1e4) {
  if (!is.finite(c) || c >= 0) return(a.max)            # degenerate: cap shape
  s  <- -c
  a0 <- (3 - s + sqrt((s - 3)^2 + 24 * s)) / (12 * s)   # Minka initial guess
  g  <- function(a) digamma(a)  - log(a) - c
  gp <- function(a) trigamma(a) - 1 / a
  # newtonRaphson can *throw* (e.g. "missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed") when an
  # iterate diverges to NaN; catch that so we fall back to a bracketed solve.
  a  <- tryCatch(
    suppressWarnings(newtonRaphson(fun = g, x0 = a0, dfun = gp,
                                   tol = tol, maxiter = maxiter)$root),
    error = function(e) NA_real_)
  if (!is.finite(a) || a <= 0 || abs(g(a)) > 1e-6)
    a <- tryCatch(uniroot(g, c(1e-8, a.max))$root, error = function(e) a.max)
  min(a, a.max)
}
```


```{r}
##' @param tauParams - the initial process precision parameters
##' @param THETA parameter matrix
##' @param dist  disturbance list: p.dist, mu0[3], V0[3,3], alloc soil

ORJointUpdate <- function(gamInit,Y,Rparams,Q,PAR,Xic,THETA,dist) {
  # initialize variables
  NT <- length(PAR)/365
  Nf = Na = array(Xic, dim = c(nrow(Xic), ncol(Xic), dist$n + 1))
  ne = nrow(Xic)
  muF <- array(NA, dim = c(dist$n + 1, 3, dist$n + 1)) 
  CF <- array(NA, dim = c(dist$n + 1, 3, 3, dist$n + 1))
  pF <- array(NA, dim = c(dist$n + 1, 3, 3, dist$n + 1))
  muA <- array(NA, dim = c(dist$n + 1, 3, dist$n + 1))
  CA <- array(NA, dim = c(dist$n + 1, 3, 3, dist$n + 1))
  likA <- array(NA, dim = c(dist$n + 1, dist$n + 1))
  gamA <- array(NA, dim = c(dist$n + 1, 2, dist$n+1))
  muFinal <- array(NA, dim=c(dist$n+1, 3))
  CFinal <- array(NA, dim=c(dist$n+1, 3, 3))
  gamFinal <- array(c(rep(gamInit[1], dist$n+1), rep(gamInit[2], dist$n+1)), dim=c(dist$n+1, 2))
  alphas <- array(NA, dim=c(dist$n+1, dist$n + 1))
  omegaA <- array(NA, dim=c(dist$n+1, dist$n + 1))
  omegaFinal <- c(0.5, rep(0.5 / dist$n, dist$n))
  
  
  if(!is.matrix(THETA)) THETA = matrix(THETA,nrow=ne,ncol=length(THETA),byrow = TRUE)
  
  H <- matrix(c(0, 0, 1), 1, 3)

  # per-timestep diagnostics for the observed wood/AGB pool (index 3)
  hist <- list(y=rep(NA,NT), overall.analysis=rep(NA,NT),
               analysis.dist=rep(NA,NT), analysis.undist=rep(NA,NT),
               forecast.dist=rep(NA,NT), forecast.undist=rep(NA,NT),
               ci.mean=rep(NA,NT), ci.lower=rep(NA,NT), ci.upper=rep(NA,NT),
               probD=rep(NA,NT),                 # posterior prob. of disturbance
               ci5=matrix(NA,NT,5),              # 5 wood-pool quantiles (2.5/25/50/75/97.5)
               nis=rep(NA,NT),                   # normalized innovation squared (wood pool)
               nis.cf=rep(NA,NT),                # S decomposition: forecast ensemble spread
               nis.q33=rep(NA,NT),               #                  process variance
               nis.R=rep(NA,NT),                 #                  observation error
               nis.innov=rep(NA,NT))             #                  innovation (y - forecast)

  for (t in 1:NT) {
    print(paste0("timestep: ", t))
    y <- Y[t, 3]
    omega.prev <- omegaFinal   # weights before this step's collapse (for forecast means)

    # No observation this timestep: forecast-only step. Run VSEM forward and add
    # process error to ALL ensemble members of every component, carry the forecast
    # ensemble forward, and skip the Kalman update / disturbance mixture / collapse.
    if (is.na(y)) {
      tsel <- (t-1)*365 + 1:365
      for (i in 1:(dist$n+1)) {
        Q[3,3] <- 1 / (gamFinal[i,1] / gamFinal[i,2])   # per-component process error
        if (!is.finite(Q[3,3]) || Q[3,3] <= 0) Q[3,3] <- 1e-6
        THETA[,9:11] <- Na[,,i]
        for (j in 1:ne) Nf[j,,i] <- VSEM(THETA[j,], PAR = PAR[tsel])[365, 2:4]
        for (j in 1:ne) Nf[j,,i] <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1, Nf[j,,i], Q)
        Na[,,i] <- Nf[,,i]                              # carry forecast forward
      }
      # record forecast-only diagnostics (no obs => analysis == forecast)
      fmean <- sapply(1:(dist$n+1), function(i) mean(Nf[,3,i]))
      fsd   <- sapply(1:(dist$n+1), function(i) sd(Nf[,3,i]))
      om <- omegaFinal; di <- 2:(dist$n+1); swd <- sum(om[di])
      hist$y[t]                <- y
      hist$forecast.undist[t]  <- fmean[1]
      hist$forecast.dist[t]    <- if (swd > 0) sum(om[di]*fmean[di])/swd else NA
      hist$overall.analysis[t] <- sum(om*fmean)
      hist$analysis.undist[t]  <- fmean[1]
      hist$analysis.dist[t]    <- hist$forecast.dist[t]
      gs <- which.max(om)
      hist$ci.mean[t]  <- fmean[gs]
      hist$ci.lower[t] <- fmean[gs] - 1.96*fsd[gs]
      hist$ci.upper[t] <- fmean[gs] + 1.96*fsd[gs]
      hist$probD[t]    <- swd
      hist$ci5[t, ]    <- normal_quantile(c(.025,.25,.5,.75,.975), fmean[gs], fsd[gs]^2)
      next
    }

    R <- Y[t, 3] * Rparams[1] + Rparams[2]

    prob.dist <- sum(dist$p[2:(dist$n + 1), t])
    prob.undist <- dist$p[1, t]
    
    for (i in 1:(dist$n+1)) {
      ## Seed VSEM ICs (foliage / soil / wood pools) with the previous timestep's
      ## analysis state for each ensemble member.
      THETA[,9:11]  <- Na[,,i]
      
      ## Deterministic forecast: run VSEM forward 365 days for each ensemble
      ## member using that year's PAR driver, and grab end-of-year pools.
      for(j in 1:ne){
        tsel    = (t-1)*365 + 1:365
        Nf[j,,i] = VSEM(THETA[j,], PAR = PAR[tsel])[365,2:4]
      }
      
      # compute process error
      Q[3, 3] <- 1 / (gamFinal[i, 1] / gamFinal[i, 2])
      if (!is.finite(Q[3, 3]) || Q[3, 3] <= 0) Q[3, 3] <- 1e-6

      
      # compute undisturbed sample mean / cov
      d.ens.p <- c(0.5, rep(0.5 / dist$n, dist$n))
      d.forecast <- rmultinom(ne, 1, d.ens.p)
      d.class <- apply(d.forecast,2,which.max) - 1
      sel.undisturbed <- which(d.class == 0)
      
      muF[1,,i] = colMeans(Nf[sel.undisturbed,,i])
      CF[1,,,i] = var(Nf[sel.undisturbed,,i])
      
      
      # add process error to undisturbed ensemble members
      for(j in sel.undisturbed) {
        Nf[j,,i] = mvtnorm::rmvnorm(1,Nf[j,,i],Q)
      }
      
      # run disturbance model on disturbed ensemble members of each class
      for (d in 1:(dist$n)) {
        sel.dist = which(d.class == d)
        # always apply the disturbance perturbation to this class's members (if any)
        for(j in sel.dist){
          Nf[j,,i] = disturbance.p(Nf[j,,i],
                      mu0=dist$vals[[d]]$mu0,
                      V0=dist$vals[[d]]$V0,
                      alloc.soil=dist$alloc.soil)
        }
        # ensemble moments only when this class has enough members (>2); else backup
        if(length(sel.dist)>2) {
          muF[d+1,,i]  = colMeans(Nf[sel.dist,,i])
          CF[d+1,,,i] = var(Nf[sel.dist,,i])
          pF[d+1,,,i] = try(solve(CF[d+1,,,i]))
        }

        if(length(sel.dist) <= 2 || "try-error" %in% class(pF[d+1,,,i]) || grepl("Error", pF[d+1, 1,1,i])) { # backup values if the ensemble stats fail
          muF[d+1,,i] = c(dist$vals[[d]]$mu0[1], mean(Nf[,2,i]),  dist$vals[[d]]$mu0[2])
          CF[d+1,,,i] = diag(c(dist$vals[[d]]$V0[1,1],0.25,dist$vals[[d]]$V0[2,2]))
          pF[d+1,,,i] = solve(CF[d+1,,,i])
          print(paste("iteration: ", d, "class: ", class(pF[d+1,1,1,i]), "value: ", pF[d+1,1,1,i]))
        }
        # pF <- array(as.numeric(pF), dim = dim(pF), dimnames = dimnames(pF))
      }
      
      # kalman update to compute means and covariances of normal components
      kalmanParams <- KalmanUpdate(muF[1,,i], CF[1,,,i] + Q, H, R, y)
      muA[1,,i] <- kalmanParams$m_hat
      CA[1,,,i] <- kalmanParams$C_hat
      likA[1,i] <- kalmanParams$L_hat
      
      for (j in 2:(dist$n+1)) {
        kalmanParams <- KalmanUpdate(muF[j,,i], CF[j,,,i], H, R, y)
        muA[j,,i] <- kalmanParams$m_hat
        CA[j,,,i] <- kalmanParams$C_hat
        likA[j,i] <- kalmanParams$L_hat
      }
      
      # no update for gamma params of disturbed components
      for (j in 2:(dist$n+1)) {
        gamA[j,,i] <- gamFinal[i,]
      }
      
      # Compute gamma params of undisturbed component via
      # Gauss-Laguerre quadrature and Newton's method
      gq <- gauss_laguerre_rate(40, gamFinal[i, 1] - 1, gamFinal[i, 2])
      
      f <- function(tau) {
        Q_tau <- diag(c(Q[1,1], Q[2,2], 1/tau))
        sd <- sqrt(R + H %*% (CF[1,,,i] + Q_tau) %*% t(H))
        normalPart <- dnorm(y, mean = H %*% muF[1,,i], sd=sd)
        gammaFactor <- (gamFinal[i, 2]**gamFinal[i, 1]) / gamma(gamFinal[i, 1])
        return(gammaFactor * normalPart)
      }
      fexp <- function(tau) tau * f(tau)
      flog <- function(tau) log(tau) * f(tau)
      
      f.integral <- integrate_gl(f, gq)
      tau.exp <- integrate_gl(fexp, gq) / f.integral
      tau.exp.log <- integrate_gl(flog, gq) / f.integral
      
      c.und <- tau.exp.log - log(tau.exp)
      if (is.finite(c.und) && c.und < 0) {
        gamA[1,1,i] <- solve_digamma_log(c.und)
        gamA[1,2,i] <- gamA[1,1,i] / tau.exp
      } else {
        # Quadrature gave no usable precision update (Jensen gap below quadrature
        # resolution); keep this component's prior Gamma params.
        warning(sprintf("undisturbed Gamma update fell back to prior at t=%d, i=%d (c=%g)",
                        t, i, c.und))
        gamA[1,,i] <- gamFinal[i,]
      }
      
      
      # branch weights = this year's per-class prior probability x data likelihood
      alphas[1, i] <- dist$p[1, t] * likA[1, i]              # undisturbed
      for (j in 2:(dist$n + 1)) {
        alphas[j, i] <- dist$p[j, t] * likA[j, i]            # each disturbance sub-class
      }

    }

    # compute component weights from this year's prior x likelihood only, so the
    # weights do not compound across years (no dependence on last year's posterior).
    component.nc <- sum(alphas)
    omegaA <- alphas / component.nc
    
    # collapse components via moment matching
    for (g in 1:(dist$n+1)) {
      sw <- sum(omegaA[g, ])
      if (!is.finite(sw) || sw <= 0) {   # component weight collapsed: keep prior, weight 0
        omegaFinal[g] <- 0
        next
      }
      wn <- omegaA[g, ] / sw            # normalized within-component (branch) weights

      m.g <- 0
      for (i in 1:(dist$n + 1)) {
        m.g <- m.g + wn[i] * muA[g,,i]
      }

      C.g <- 0
      for (i in 1:(dist$n + 1)) {
        C.g <- C.g + wn[i] * (CA[g,,,i] + (muA[g,,i] - m.g) %*% t(muA[g,,i] - m.g))
      }

      tau.exp <- 0
      tau.logexp <- 0
      for (i in 1:(dist$n + 1)) {
        tau.exp <- tau.exp + wn[i] * (gamA[g,1,i] / gamA[g, 2, i])
        tau.logexp <- tau.logexp + wn[i] * (digamma(gamA[g, 1, i]) - log(gamA[g, 2, i]))
      }
      
      c.g <- tau.logexp - log(tau.exp)
      if (is.finite(c.g) && c.g < 0) {
        a.g <- solve_digamma_log(c.g)
        b.g <- a.g / tau.exp
      } else {
        warning(sprintf("collapse Gamma update fell back to prior at t=%d, g=%d (c=%g)", t, g, c.g))
        a.g <- gamFinal[g,1]
        b.g <- gamFinal[g,2]
      }

      muFinal[g,] <- m.g
      CFinal[g,,] <- C.g
      gamFinal[g,1] <- a.g
      gamFinal[g,2] <- b.g
      omegaFinal[g] <- sw
      
    }
    
    # update analysis ensemble: reseed each component's IC ensemble from its collapsed
    # analysis Gaussian N(muFinal[g,], CFinal[g,,]). Symmetrize and add a little noise to
    # the covariance (additive inflation) so the draw stays positive-definite and the
    # ensemble spread cannot collapse. Sample via SVD for robustness to near-singular cov.
    infl <- 0.02                                   # relative noise added per pool
    for (g in 1:(dist$n+1)) {
      Cg <- (CFinal[g,,] + t(CFinal[g,,])) / 2     # symmetrize
      Cg <- Cg + diag((infl * muFinal[g,])^2 + 1e-8, 3)   # add noise for stability
      Na[,,g] <- mvtnorm::rmvnorm(ne, mean = muFinal[g,], sigma = Cg, method = "svd")
    }
    Na <- pmax(Na, 1e-6)                           # keep carbon pools positive

    # record analysis/forecast diagnostics (wood pool = index 3).
    # muFinal[g,]/CFinal[g,,] are the conditional mean/cov; weight by omegaFinal for mixtures.
    # Exclude dead components (om == 0) whose stored muFinal is stale.
    om <- omegaFinal; di <- 2:(dist$n+1)
    live <- which(om > 0); lived <- di[om[di] > 0]; swd <- sum(om[lived])
    hist$y[t]                <- y
    hist$overall.analysis[t] <- sum(om[live] * muFinal[live, 3])  # mixture mean
    hist$analysis.undist[t]  <- if (om[1] > 0) muFinal[1,3] else NA
    hist$analysis.dist[t]    <- if (swd > 0) sum(om[lived] * muFinal[lived,3]) / swd else NA
    gs  <- which.max(om)
    cm  <- muFinal[gs,3]
    sdg <- sqrt(max(CFinal[gs,3,3], 0))
    hist$ci.mean[t]  <- cm
    hist$ci.lower[t] <- cm - 1.96*sdg
    hist$ci.upper[t] <- cm + 1.96*sdg
    hist$probD[t]    <- swd                                       # posterior prob. of disturbance
    hist$ci5[t, ]    <- normal_quantile(c(.025,.25,.5,.75,.975), cm, max(CFinal[gs,3,3], 0))
    hist$forecast.undist[t] <- sum(omega.prev * muF[1,3,])       # branch-weighted, undisturbed
    fc.d <- 0; for (j in di) fc.d <- fc.d + sum(omega.prev * muF[j,3,])
    hist$forecast.dist[t]   <- fc.d / dist$n                     # uniform over disturbed classes

    ## normalized innovation squared (wood pool): pick the single dominant forecast
    ## component by POSTERIOR weight (omegaA, after likelihood) so a flagged-but-poorly-
    ## fitting disturbance class is not forced when the data contradict it. Innovation
    ## cov = H C^f H^T + R for that one component (undisturbed adds its Q[3,3]).
    if (all(!is.finite(omegaA)) || max(omegaA, na.rm = TRUE) <= 0) {
      hist$nis[t] <- NA
    } else {
      idx   <- which(omegaA == max(omegaA, na.rm = TRUE), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
      gstar <- idx[1]; istar <- idx[2]
      q33 <- if (gstar == 1) { v <- 1/(gamFinal[istar,1]/gamFinal[istar,2]); if (!is.finite(v) || v <= 0) 1e-6 else v } else 0
      S <- CF[gstar,3,3,istar] + q33 + R
      hist$nis[t] <- if (is.finite(S) && S > 0) (y - muF[gstar,3,istar])^2 / S else NA
      ## store the S decomposition so nis.cf + nis.q33 + nis.R == S exactly
      hist$nis.cf[t]    <- CF[gstar,3,3,istar]
      hist$nis.q33[t]   <- q33
      hist$nis.R[t]     <- R
      hist$nis.innov[t] <- y - muF[gstar,3,istar]
    }

  }

  return(hist)
}

```

```{r}
## Generate ORJointUpdate inputs for each requested site, run the joint update,
## and save each site's diagnostics to experiments/jointUpdate. Returns the
## results invisibly (keyed by site) for convenience.
## Rparams.source ("GEDI"/"LandTrendr") and Rparams.model ("het"/"con") describe the
## observation-error parameters in use; they are recorded in each output filename.
run_joint_update_sites <- function(site.idx, Rparams = Rparams.GEDI.het,
                                   useDistProduct = TRUE,
                                   Rparams.source = c("GEDI", "LandTrendr"),
                                   Rparams.model  = c("het", "con"),
                                   outdir = "experiments/jointUpdateYear15") {
  Rparams.source <- match.arg(Rparams.source)
  Rparams.model  <- match.arg(Rparams.model)
  if (!dir.exists(outdir)) dir.create(outdir, recursive = TRUE)
  results <- list()
  for (site in site.idx) {
    message("running joint update for site ", site)
    args <- make_or_args(site, useDistProduct)
    out <- ORJointUpdate(gamInit = gamInit, Y = args$Y, Rparams = Rparams,
                         Q = Q, PAR = args$PAR, Xic = ICprior,
                         THETA = theta[1:11], dist = args$disturb.params)
    fname <- file.path(outdir,
                       sprintf("site_%d_distprod_%s_%s_%s.rds",
                               site, useDistProduct, Rparams.source, Rparams.model))
    saveRDS(out, fname)
    results[[as.character(site)]] <- out
  }
  invisible(results)
}
```

```{r}
run_joint_update_sites(site.idx = seq(1, ne, by=1), Rparams = Rparams.GEDI.het, useDistProduct = TRUE,
                       Rparams.source = "GEDI", Rparams.model = "het")
```

```{r}
run_joint_update_sites(site.idx = seq(1, ne, by=1), Rparams = Rparams.GEDI.fixed, useDistProduct = TRUE,
                       Rparams.source = "GEDI", Rparams.model = "con")

                       Rparams.source = "LandTrendr", Rparams.model = "con")
```

```{r}
# Plot wood/AGB pool trajectories: observation, analysis & forecast means
# (overall / disturbed / undisturbed), and the 95% CI of the most likely component.
res <- readRDS("experiments/jointUpdate/site_391_distprod_TRUE_GEDI_het.rds")
tt <- seq_along(res$y)
ylim <- range(c(res$y, res$ci.lower, res$ci.upper, res$overall.analysis,
                res$analysis.dist, res$analysis.undist,
                res$forecast.dist, res$forecast.undist), na.rm=TRUE)
plot(tt, res$overall.analysis, type="n", ylim=ylim,
     xlab="timestep (year)", ylab="wood / AGB pool (kg C m-2)",
     main="OR joint update - wood pool")
ok <- is.finite(res$ci.lower) & is.finite(res$ci.upper)
polygon(c(tt[ok], rev(tt[ok])), c(res$ci.lower[ok], rev(res$ci.upper[ok])),
        col=adjustcolor("grey70", 0.4), border=NA)
lines(tt, res$overall.analysis, col="black",       lwd=2)
lines(tt, res$analysis.undist,  col="forestgreen", lwd=2)
#lines(tt, res$analysis.dist,    col="firebrick",   lwd=2)
lines(tt, res$forecast.undist,  col="forestgreen", lwd=1, lty=2)
lines(tt, res$forecast.dist,    col="firebrick",   lwd=1, lty=2)
points(tt, res$y, pch=19, col="blue")
legend("topleft", bty="n", cex=0.8,
  legend=c("Y (obs)","overall analysis","analysis undist","analysis dist",
           "forecast undist","forecast dist","95% CI (top comp)"),
  col=c("blue","black","forestgreen","firebrick","forestgreen","firebrick","grey70"),
  pch=c(19,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,15), lty=c(NA,1,1,1,2,2,NA), lwd=c(NA,2,2,2,1,1,NA))
```
